experiences.title: Fetch-execute factory
experiences.description: Step inside the CPU and follow an instruction through the fetch-decode-execute cycle. Includes a 3D CPU you can take apart.

experiences.title: Von Neumann HQ
experiences.description: Meet John von Neumann and explore the stored-program architecture inside nearly every computer. Includes a 3D model of the architecture.

experiences.title: Speed lab
experiences.description: Find out how clock speed, cache size and number of cores affect CPU performance. Includes a 3D multi-core CPU and a motherboard with cooling.

experiences.title: Smart home
experiences.description: Find the embedded systems hidden around a smart home, and take apart a 3D washing machine to see the computer inside.

experiences.title: End-of-topic test
experiences.description: Your 1.1 test is done on paper. Revisit the lessons you found hardest first, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Memory bay
experiences.description: Primary storage up close: what RAM and ROM do, and why one forgets everything when you switch off.

experiences.title: Swap space
experiences.description: What happens when RAM runs out: paging, virtual memory and why the computer grinds to a halt.

experiences.title: Storage warehouse
experiences.description: Why computers need secondary storage, and how magnetic, optical and solid state devices actually work.

experiences.title: Top Trumps
experiences.description: Compare storage devices on capacity, speed, portability, durability, reliability and cost.

experiences.title: Pick the storage
experiences.description: Nine real situations, from distributing a film to backing up photos: choose the right device and justify it.

experiences.title: Units lab
experiences.description: From a single bit to a petabyte: why computers use binary, and how to convert between the units.

experiences.title: Capacity calculator
experiences.description: Work out how much storage images, sound and text really need, and how many files will fit.

experiences.title: Binary workshop
experiences.description: Convert between denary and 8-bit binary, add binary numbers, and see what happens when they overflow.

experiences.title: Assessment 1
experiences.description: Your first 1.2 test is done on paper. Warm up with Binary blitz, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Shift and hex lab
experiences.description: Multiply and divide with binary shifts, and learn why programmers write binary in hexadecimal.

experiences.title: Revision HQ 1.2 part 1
experiences.description: Recap lessons 1 to 10: memory, storage, units, capacity, binary, shifts and hexadecimal.

experiences.title: Character foundry
experiences.description: How text becomes binary: character sets, ASCII and Unicode, and why more bits means more characters.

experiences.title: Pixel studio
experiences.description: Colour pixels and watch the bits add up: resolution, colour depth, metadata and image file size.

experiences.title: Sound studio
experiences.description: Turn a sound wave into binary: sampling, sample rate, bit depth, and the effect on quality and file size.

experiences.title: Compression works
experiences.description: Why files are compressed, the difference between lossy and lossless, and run-length encoding in action.

experiences.title: Revision HQ 1.2 part 2
experiences.description: Recap lessons 12 to 15: character sets, images, sound and compression, ready for the second test.

experiences.title: Assessment 2
experiences.description: Your second 1.2 test is done on paper. Revise with Revision HQ part 2, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Binary blitz
experiences.description: Two minutes of denary, binary and hexadecimal conversions against the clock, with speed bonuses and streaks. Replay to beat your personal best.

experiences.title: Types of network: zoom out
experiences.description: Zoom out from one computer to a school LAN and the whole world. Standalone computers, LANs and WANs.

experiences.title: Network control room
experiences.description: Take charge of a slow school network and find the five factors that affect performance.

experiences.title: Network showdown
experiences.description: Client-server takes on peer-to-peer: who does what in each model, and which one suits a school, an office or a file share.

experiences.title: Mission: wire up the school
experiences.description: Explore a school server room and find the hardware that connects a LAN.

experiences.title: Inside the internet
experiences.description: Find out what the internet really is, how DNS finds websites, and what hosting and the cloud mean.

experiences.title: Star and mesh networks
experiences.description: Break a star network, then see how full, partial and wireless mesh networks compare.

experiences.title: Revision HQ
experiences.description: Recap lessons 1 to 6 and find out what to revise before your mid-topic test.

experiences.title: Assessment 1
experiences.description: Your 1.3 test on lessons 1 to 7 is done on paper. Warm up first with Revision HQ, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Connection café
experiences.description: Ethernet, Wi-Fi or Bluetooth? Compare wired and wireless connections and recommend the right one for each job.

experiences.title: Cipher room
experiences.description: Crack a cipher, learn how keys work, and find out how Wi-Fi keeps your data secret with WPA2.

experiences.title: Address sorting office
experiences.description: Sort MAC, IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, and find out why the world needed IPv6.

experiences.title: Protocol city
experiences.description: Explore the standards and protocols that make networks work, from HTTP to TCP/IP.

experiences.title: Parcel depot
experiences.description: Follow a parcel from box to sack to van, and find out why layering protocols makes networks easier to build.

experiences.title: Revision HQ 2
experiences.description: Recap lessons 9 to 13 and find out what to revise before your end-of-unit assessment.

experiences.title: Assessment 2 reflection
experiences.description: Once your end-of-unit test is marked, use this sheet to plan what to improve.

experiences.title: Threat map
experiences.description: Meet the six forms of attack on the OCR specification, find out why attackers do it, and follow the CryptoLocker story.

experiences.title: Malware lab
experiences.description: Study viruses, worms, trojans, ransomware and spyware under the microscope, and learn how to stop them.

experiences.title: Database break-in
experiences.description: See how a single quotation mark in a login box can hand over a database, and learn how programmers stop it.

experiences.title: Phishing inbox
experiences.description: Work through a suspicious inbox: learn what phishing is, what attackers gain, and how to spot the signs.

experiences.title: Social engineering HQ
experiences.description: People are the weakest link: blagging, shouldering, baiting and the everyday habits that let attackers in.

experiences.title: Cracking lab
experiences.description: See how fast a computer can guess passwords, and learn what makes a password, and a login page, hard to crack.

experiences.title: Traffic flood
experiences.description: Watch a website drown under fake traffic: DoS, DDoS, botnets and zombies, and the day half the internet went down.

experiences.title: Packet sniffers
experiences.description: Data can be read as it travels. Learn how interception works, what it gives attackers, and how encryption stops it.

experiences.title: Defence depot
experiences.description: The first four prevention methods: penetration testing, anti-malware, firewalls and user access levels.

experiences.title: Defence depot 2
experiences.description: Passwords, encryption and physical security, and choosing the right defence for each threat.

experiences.title: End-of-topic test
experiences.description: Your 1.4 test is done on paper. Warm up with the Cyber defence game, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Cyber defence
experiences.description: Spend a budget on protections, identify each incoming threat and find out whether your defences hold. Three lives, then the network shuts down.

experiences.title: Control room
experiences.description: What an operating system is for, and the four kinds of user interface you need to know.

experiences.title: Multitasking floor
experiences.description: How one processor appears to run everything at once, how memory is shared out, and why drivers exist.

experiences.title: Accounts office
experiences.description: User accounts, access levels and permissions, and how an operating system keeps files organised.

experiences.title: Utility workshop
experiences.description: The utility programs that keep a computer healthy: encryption, defragmentation and compression.

experiences.title: End of topic test
experiences.description: Your 1.5 test is done on paper. Revise with the four experiences first, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Impact desk
experiences.description: The six kinds of impact every new technology has, and how to argue an ethical question properly.

experiences.title: Privacy lab
experiences.description: What is collected about you, who gets it, and where the line between useful and intrusive sits.

experiences.title: Law court
experiences.description: The three Acts you need: data protection, computer misuse, and copyright, and which one applies.

experiences.title: Culture street
experiences.description: How technology changed daily life, who gets left behind, and what globalisation did to work.

experiences.title: Planet works
experiences.description: The environmental cost of a device across its whole life: making it, running it and throwing it away.

experiences.title: Stakeholder room
experiences.description: Reading a scenario the way an examiner does: who the stakeholders are, and the local, national and global effects.

experiences.title: Licence lab
experiences.description: Open source and proprietary software: what each licence allows, and which suits a given situation.

experiences.title: End of topic test
experiences.description: Your 1.6 test is done on paper. Revise with the seven experiences and the Name that Act challenge, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Name that Act
experiences.description: Two minutes of real cases: name the Act each one falls under, with speed bonuses and streaks. Some break no law at all.

experiences.title: Abstraction studio
experiences.description: Stripping a problem back to what matters, and why every useful model leaves things out.

experiences.title: Breakdown bay
experiences.description: Splitting a large problem into parts small enough to solve, and drawing the result as a structure diagram.

experiences.title: Algorithm workshop
experiences.description: Thinking in steps: inputs, processes and outputs, and what makes a set of instructions an algorithm.

experiences.title: Flowchart factory
experiences.description: The five flowchart symbols, and how to draw an algorithm that anyone can follow.

experiences.title: Pseudocode press
experiences.description: Writing algorithms in pseudocode, and reading the OCR reference language you meet in the exam.

experiences.title: Search corridor
experiences.description: The linear search: simple, works on anything, and slow when the list gets long.

experiences.title: Halving hall
experiences.description: The binary search: throw away half the list every time, but only if the list is sorted.

experiences.title: Bubble bay
experiences.description: The bubble sort: compare neighbours, swap them if they are the wrong way round, and repeat.

experiences.title: Split and insert
experiences.description: Two faster sorts: merge sort, which splits the list right down, and insertion sort, which builds order as it goes.

experiences.title: Fault finder
experiences.description: Syntax errors and logic errors: telling them apart, spotting them in code, and suggesting a fix.

experiences.title: Trace room
experiences.description: Trace tables: following a program by hand, one line at a time, to see exactly what it does.

experiences.title: End of topic test
experiences.description: Your 2.1 test is done on paper. Revise with the eleven experiences and the Algorithm arena, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Algorithm arena
experiences.description: Two minutes of searches to run, sorts to complete and bugs to find, with speed bonuses and streaks. The challenges get harder as you go.

experiences.title: Tuck shop till
experiences.description: Write your first working programs: print to the screen, store values in variables, read what the user types and cast between data types.

experiences.title: Number workshop
experiences.description: Every arithmetic operator you need: add, subtract, multiply, divide, integer division, modulus, powers, rounding and random numbers.

experiences.title: Decision gate
experiences.description: Selection from the ground up: comparisons, if, else, elif, the logical operators and decisions nested inside other decisions.

experiences.title: Lap counter
experiences.description: Count-controlled iteration: the for loop, the range it counts through, running totals and loops nested inside other loops.

experiences.title: Waiting room
experiences.description: Condition-controlled iteration: while loops, validation loops that ask again, sentinel values and choosing between for and while.

experiences.title: Letter press
experiences.description: String handling: length and position, slicing, upper and lower case, searching inside text and the character codes behind every letter.

experiences.title: Stock shelves
experiences.description: One-dimensional arrays: making a list, reading an item by its index, traversing it, adding and removing items, and totals and averages.

experiences.title: Seating plan hall
experiences.description: Two-dimensional arrays: a list of lists, reading a cell by row and column, nested loops over a grid, and totalling rows and columns.

experiences.title: Assembly line
experiences.description: Subprograms: writing a procedure, passing values in through parameters, returning a value, and the difference between local and global variables.

experiences.title: Records office
experiences.description: File handling: opening a file, reading it whole or line by line, the write and append modes, and splitting a line of records into its fields.

experiences.title: Sorting depot
experiences.description: Code the standard algorithms yourself: linear and binary search, then bubble, insertion and merge sort, and count the comparisons each one needs.

experiences.title: Gatehouse
experiences.description: Write the validation a robust program needs: presence, type, range, length and format checks, loops that keep asking, and authentication.

experiences.title: Query desk
experiences.description: Ask a database a question with SQL: SELECT and FROM, filtering with WHERE, comparing values, joining conditions with AND and OR, and sorting with ORDER BY.

experiences.title: Security desk
experiences.description: Check every sign-up at the security desk: learn the validation checks that stop bad data getting in.

experiences.title: Cyber defence HQ
experiences.description: Defend a program against misuse, bots and weak passwords with authentication and defensive design.

experiences.title: Code clinic
experiences.description: Diagnose unreadable code, learn the habits that make programs maintainable, and refine an algorithm to make it robust.

experiences.title: Bug hunt lab
experiences.description: Find out why and when programs are tested, and learn to tell syntax errors from logic errors.

experiences.title: Test lab
experiences.description: Choose normal, boundary, invalid and erroneous test data, and build a test table that really tests a program.

experiences.title: Revision HQ 2.3
experiences.description: Recap lessons 1 to 5 of Producing robust programs and find out what to revise before your test.

experiences.title: End-of-topic test
experiences.description: Your 2.3 test is done on paper. Warm up first with Revision HQ 2.3, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Logic gate lab
experiences.description: Meet AND, OR and NOT, fill in their truth tables, then build your own logic circuits by dragging gates and wires.

experiences.title: Truth table detectives
experiences.description: Crack two- and three-input truth tables, including intermediate columns, and work out logic from electric circuits.

experiences.title: Circuit workshop
experiences.description: Turn real scenarios into logic circuits and truth tables: a shop alarm, a hospital lift and a greenhouse heater.

experiences.title: End-of-topic test
experiences.description: Your 2.4 test is done on paper. Warm up with Logic sprint first, then use this reflection sheet once it's marked.

experiences.title: Logic sprint
experiences.description: Two minutes, random circuits and expressions, speed bonuses and streaks. Replay as often as you like to beat your personal best.

experiences.title: Language level lab
experiences.description: Compare high-level and low-level languages, explain why translation is needed and justify a language choice.

experiences.title: Language choice workshop
experiences.description: Choose a language level for different projects and explain the benefits and drawbacks of each choice.

experiences.title: Translation studio
experiences.description: Follow source code through translation and choose a compiler or interpreter for different working situations.

experiences.title: IDE control room
experiences.description: Explore the four main IDE facilities and explain how they help programmers write, translate and run programs.

experiences.title: Language review HQ
experiences.description: Apply the whole topic to short scenarios, check your reasoning and use review mode to repair misunderstandings.
